intent: The land-speed trap: everyone says cheetah, but the peregrine's hunting dive triples it — shown as speed blocks against a motorway car, a falcon rising out of the US where the record was measured, and a city-to-city pin pair for the comeback.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which animal is the FASTEST on Earth?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which animal is the fastest on Earth?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The peregrine falcon. In a hunting dive it has been clocked at 389 kilometres an hour.

lines.direction: hold on the US; three speed blocks rise on 'cheetah' — falcon, cheetah, motorway car — the cheetah sticker on 'cheetah', the car sticker on 'car', a flash and a pulse on 'triples'
lines.text: A cheetah tops out near 112. A car on the motorway does 110. The falcon triples both.

lines.direction: push into the Pacific Northwest; the tag on 'Washington'; on 'Frightful' the falcon sticker RISES out of the United States like a pop-up; the parachute sticker on 'skydiver'
lines.text: That record dive was measured over Washington State, where a falcon named Frightful dived alongside a skydiver.

lines.direction: pull out across the Atlantic; the skull sticker on 'pesticides'; the building sticker on 'skyscrapers'; New York pin + tag on 'York', London pin on 'London'
lines.text: Pesticides nearly wiped them out in the 1960s. Today they nest on skyscrapers, from New York to London.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Faster than you thought. Follow us.
